clue.text: Loud knocker cut short, appearing chilled

parts.note: F is forte, the musical abbreviation for loud

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: a rapper is a door knocker

explanation.surface: A noisy door knocker gets trimmed and comes out cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Frappé describes a drink served iced, so it means chilled.

clue.text: Elizabeth divorced from Nick about to go berserk

indicators.note: about means the remainder is turned round
divorced from means those letters are separated out

parts.note: to nick is to steal or pilfer
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: Elizabeth splits from Nick and he goes mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip is informal for losing one's temper or going crazy.

clue.text: Having endless cunning, brings up children in debt

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: art can mean cunning or craft
to rear is to bring up young

explanation.surface: A crafty parent raising a family runs into debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link, giving 'in arrears' for 'in debt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrears are money owed and overdue, a debt.

clue.text: Early showings of seats the right (virtually corrupt) held

indicators.note: held means the pews contain other letters

parts.note: pews are church seats
R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: virtually means almost all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: evil means wicked or corrupt

explanation.surface: Benches hold up the nearly corrupt right in political sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: Previews are showings of a film or play before its official opening.

clue.text: Country where adolescent converted having dispensed with drugs

indicators.note: converted says the letters of adolescent are changed into a new arrangement

parts.note: E stands for ecstasy, so drugs are Es

explanation.surface: A teenager in some land reforms after giving up drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having dispensed with' tells you two Es (drugs) come out of the scrambled letters of ADOLESCENT, leaving the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland is a country of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Traveller inordinately rich — don't let her get away!

indicators.note: inordinately suggests the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
the plea 'stop her' asks for her to be halted

explanation.surface: A wealthy traveller begs that a woman be stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: St Christopher is the patron saint of travellers, and Christopher Columbus a famous traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Christopher is the patron of travellers, so the name stands for one.

clue.text: Bleak prospect, one difficult to crack, heading off heavenwards

indicators.note: heavenwards means going up, so in a down clue the letters read from bottom to top
heading off means the first letter goes

parts.note: a hard nut is a person or problem tough to crack

explanation.surface: A forbidding view of a tough nut climbing upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is a vast, treeless arctic plain, a bleak landscape.

clue.text: Unreliable man I love, the heartless reptile, perhaps

indicators.note: unreliable suggests the letters will not stay in place

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

explanation.surface: A fickle man declares love to a cold-blooded creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Amniotes are animals whose embryos grow in an amnion, such as reptiles, birds and mammals.

clue.text: Motion to strike in the southwest in street of government

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Downing Street is the home of the British prime minister
SW is the abbreviation for southwest

explanation.surface: A move to strike goes on in Westminster.
explanation.definitionFit: A downswing is the downward movement of a club or bat to hit the ball.

clue.text: Where Ariel Sharon's heading for reform, disorder or disaster

indicators.note: three words of upheaval all say the letters are to be thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, here of Sharon's

explanation.surface: A comment on the troubled country led by the Israeli prime minister Ariel Sharon.
explanation.walkthrough: Ariel Sharon was Israel's prime minister when the puzzle appeared, so the surface reads as political comment.
explanation.definitionFit: Where is a bare place question, answered by the nation the surface is about.

clue.text: Tea's gathered and at end of season freshly made

indicators.note: gathered means the brew collects other letters inside it

parts.note: a brew is a pot of tea; the 's stands for has
taken as written

indicators.note: at end of picks the last letter of season

explanation.surface: A late-season pot of tea is freshly prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brand new has just been made and is unused.

clue.text: Mother marrying men admits "I'm such a nightmare, they're picked to send me delirious"

definitions.text: they're picked to send me delirious

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: admits means the grooms let other letters in

parts.note: grooms are men getting married

indicators.note: a nightmare suggests the letters are in a terrible muddle

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A mother at a wedding confesses she is a nightmare.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface looks like a bride's quoted confession; the quote marks are just there to hide the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallucinogenic fungi are gathered wild and eaten to bring on delirium.

clue.text: Beastly accommodation for Spooner's beast with squeaky voice on steroids?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first letters change places

parts.note: a squeak pumped up becomes a honk, so a honkey voice
a mouse is a small beast

explanation.surface: A mouse whose squeak has been pumped up by steroids is pictured.
explanation.walkthrough: A HONKEY MOUSE is a mouse whose squeak has grown to a honk; swap the H and M.
explanation.definitionFit: The monkey house at a zoo is where the animals are kept, a home for beasts.

clue.text: Embellished, transparent feature of rude words one passed round the Caribbean?

indicators.note: passed round says the scrambled letters go around another piece
rude here means rough and unformed, so the letters are knocked into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
WI is the West Indies, the Caribbean islands

explanation.surface: Rude words are circulated among Caribbean folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude' means rough here, not obscene. 'passed round' puts the shuffled letters around WI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose window is a round, decorated stained-glass window in a church.

clue.text: Codgers to maintain "The Queen's Head", maybe, in places where the Queen isn't!

indicators.note: to maintain means the relics hold something within them

parts.note: old codgers can be called relics, people from a past age
the Queen's Head is a typical British pub name

explanation.surface: Old men keep the local going in countries without a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's Head is a common British pub name, given as an example by 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Republics are states with an elected head rather than a monarch.

clue.text: Island accommodating non-revolutionary material

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Victoria's work about to be given to mum

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
mum means keep quiet, which sh demands

explanation.surface: Victoria Beckham's latest output reaches her mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria Beckham was Posh Spice; 'to be given to' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria Beckham's Spice Girls nickname was Posh.

clue.text: One could be obsessed with training, bearing Harry

definitions.text: One could be obsessed with training

parts.note: S, for south, is a compass bearing
Harry Potter is the boy wizard

explanation.surface: A fitness fanatic carries Harry Potter around.

explanation.definitionFit: A trainspotter is obsessed with logging trains, a spotter.

clue.text: In marriage to socialist she gave _____ to provide a diversion

parts.note: red is a common term for a socialist
her is the object form of she
a ring symbolises marriage

explanation.surface: A woman married to a leftist gives something to throw people off.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is the answer itself; the pieces come in the order red, her, ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a misleading clue meant to distract attention.

clue.text: Imagines one goes out with potential partners, trapping a quarter

indicators.note: trapping means the dates enclose a letter

parts.note: to date is to go out with possible partners
E for east is one quarter of the compass

explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form ideas, to imagine.

clue.text: Might one smoke forty a day? Rebelliously, did indeed

definitions.text: Might one smoke forty a day?

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an act

indicators.note: rebelliously suggests the letters revolt and change order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is a heavy smoker and gets an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smoking forty a day is hooked, a nicotine addict.

clue.text: "Gore more favoured to British Lord", 'e cursed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone swears while giving Gore a better chance than a British peer.
explanation.walkthrough: Gore looks like Al Gore, but it means bloodshed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bloodthirstier means being keener on bloodshed than another.

clue.text: One's mildly tasteful and, though somewhat aged, amazing!

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of these words is used

explanation.surface: Praise for something tasteful and amazing though aged.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild-flavoured Dutch cheese.

clue.text: Clandestine affair for which pair of eyes sounded urgent, possibly

parts.note: two eyes said out loud are two letter Is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A secret romance where the lovers' glances seemed pressing.
explanation.definitionFit: An intrigue can be a secret love affair, as well as a plot.

clue.text: Married to eleven men, perhaps?

explanation.surface: A woman wed to a whole football team.
explanation.walkthrough: Many British football clubs are called United, such as Manchester United, and a team has eleven men.
explanation.definitionFit: Married people are joined, and many football teams carry this name.

clue.text: Safeguarded money certain to go to family?

parts.note: sure means certain
family ties are the bonds of kin

explanation.surface: Secure savings are sure to pass to relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Sureties are sums pledged as guarantees, money held as security.

clue.text: Black man all washed up?

parts.note: jet black is a deep black
